why: (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: CONFIRMED. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup.md puts the sentence at line 275, byte-identical. Read the WHOLE line: it is three sentences, not two, and the uncited third reinforces rather than reverses -- 'Use this when you distribute Claude Code through your own channels and need users to stay on the version you provide.' Section context (:263 '### Disable auto-updates', :265-273 the settings.json env block) confirms the reading. But that third sentence is also what breaks the finding, because it names the exact deployment posture this fork already occupies. (2) CITED LINES: partially confirmed, with one dead line. auto-update.ts:130 `autoUpdater.autoInstallOnAppQuit = true` is genuinely an unconditional module-level assignment. auto-update.ts:47 is indeed the sole `process.env` read (`process.env.LOCALAPPDATA` in getUpdateCacheDir). But auto-update.ts:127 `autoUpdater.autoDownload = true` is a DEAD default: checkForUpdates() overwrites it at :334 from its own parameter and restores the previous value at :369 on every single check, and all four call sites pass an explicit `{autoDownload: true}` (auto-update.ts:448, menu.ts:75, menu.ts:200, handlers/system.ts:274). Deleting :127 changes nothing. The grep is accurate -- `grep -rain -e DISABLE_UPDATE -e DISABLE_AUTOUPDAT --include='*.ts' packages apps scripts` returns 0, and a repo-wide `grep -ain` across ts/tsx/json/md/mjs/js/yml finds the strings only inside this sweep's own artefacts. So the IDENTIFIER half of the claim is true. (3) LAYER UP AND DOWN -- the CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier, is FALSE, on two independent grounds. LAYER UP: there is no vendor-run update feed to opt out of. apps/electron/electron-builder.yml:77-80 sets `publish: {provider: generic, url: "${env.NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_URL}", channel: "${env.NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_CHANNEL}"}`, injected at build time from the deploying organisation's own CI secret (.gitlab-ci.yml:234-235, `export NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_URL="$NESSY_DESKTOP_DEV_UPDATE_URL"`; apps/electron/README.md:79 shows the same knob for local rehearsal). In Claude Code, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER/DISABLE_UPDATES exist because Anthropic runs the feed and the redistributing org does not -- the flags are how the org takes the vendor's updater out of the loop. Here the premise is inverted: the organisation that deploys Nessy Desktop is the organisation that builds it (AGENTS.md: internal desktop-agent fork rebranded for T-Bank), and it already decides which version every user can reach by controlling what it publishes to its own feed. A build with no URL has no working provider at all (GenericProvider.js:12 passes configuration.url straight to newBaseUrl). So the claimed harm -- 'A corporate deployment cannot pin users to a distributed version' -- is false; pinning is the fork's structural default, achieved by the mechanism the quoted third sentence prescribes rather than by an env flag. Also relevant one layer up: the launch probe is gated on `app.isPackaged` (index.ts:1259-1265, else-branch logs '[auto-update] Skipping auto-update in dev mode'), so even 'hardcoded on' is not literally unconditional. LAYER DOWN / SIBLING SUBSYSTEM: DISABLE_UPDATES is distinguished from DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER by exactly one thing -- blocking the MANUAL paths `claude update` and `claude install`, i.e. the native installer that manages ~/.local/bin/claude as a symlink into ~/.local/share/claude/versions/ (setup.md:205, :277-293). Nessy Desktop has no native installer, no versions/ directory and no self-update subcommand: apps/cli/src/index.ts parses only flags (--url, --token, --model, --version, ...) with no `update` or `install` verb, and `grep -rain -e self-update -e selfUpdate apps/cli/src` returns nothing. The entire reason the second flag exists as a separate flag has no counterpart to diverge from. Measuring a CLI-installer two-flag contract against an Electron electron-updater subsystem is the sibling-subsystem error this series warns about. (4) NOT an inert-worklist section 3 owner decision -- the nine are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions; none is this. (5) It IS partly a deliberate product difference: desktop Electron app with a build-time-injected generic feed vs a self-updating CLI binary. Refuted on the consequence, not on the identifier.
correctedState: Neither `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` nor `DISABLE_UPDATES` nor a NESSY_-prefixed runtime equivalent is read -- that part is accurate (0 hits repo-wide with `grep -a`). Three corrections to the rest. (a) The evidence line is wrong: auto-update.ts:127 `autoUpdater.autoDownload = true` is a dead default, overwritten at :334 and restored at :369 on every check while all four call sites pass an explicit `{autoDownload: true}` (auto-update.ts:448, menu.ts:75, menu.ts:200, handlers/system.ts:274); the only operative unconditional assignment is :130 (`autoInstallOnAppQuit`), and the launch probe itself is gated on `app.isPackaged` at index.ts:1259. (b) The claimed harm is false. Update behaviour IS organisation-controlled here, just at build time rather than runtime: electron-builder.yml:77-80 bakes `publish.provider: generic` with `url`/`channel` from `NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_URL` / `NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_CHANNEL`, supplied by the deploying org's own CI (.gitlab-ci.yml:234-235). There is no Anthropic-equivalent vendor feed to opt out of -- the org that ships the build owns the feed and pins users by controlling what it publishes to it, which is exactly the 'distribute through your own channels' posture the quoted sentence's third clause prescribes. (c) `DISABLE_UPDATES`'s distinguishing purpose -- blocking `claude update` / `claude install` and the native installer under ~/.local/share/claude/versions/ -- has no analogue: apps/cli/src/index.ts exposes no `update` or `install` subcommand and nothing in this fork self-updates a CLI binary. The genuine residual, narrower than the finding as filed, is that a PACKAGED build has no runtime off switch: an admin cannot suppress the per-launch probe or the user-facing 'Check for Updates' menu item (menu.ts:75) and Settings 'Check Now' (AppSettingsPage.tsx:149) without a rebuild, and there is no settings toggle (the only `disabled` in that page is the in-flight spinner guard at :457). That residual overlaps f189 and f202, which cite the same two lines.
